title: IOP Standard or Workflow Operation
description: A reusable composition of operations saved in the laboratory. Basic Operations are the operations of registered devices. Give steps and result, or, for a Workflow Operation that decides from results, send program files with the definition.

layer.description: standard: a reusable method built from Basic and Standard Operations. workflow: an organization of methods across devices; it may use all three.

conditions.description: When the result has its stated meaning

parameters.description: name -> {type, minimum, maximum, enum, default, required, unit}

device.description: Device whose operation is called (a Basic Operation). Omit it to use a saved Standard or Workflow Operation named by operation.

repeat.description: Run the step this many times in turn, at each point of its sweep if it has one; what it returns is gathered over a last axis named repeat, or "${name}" for a parameter

steps.description: Run in the order written; after: [] starts a parallel branch. "${name}" in arguments or device inserts a parameter.

result.description: name -> {step, path, view}: the values the operation returns; with view, path selects inside a view of an array the step returned

program.description: Set by the Runtime from the program files: command, files, sha256 and bytes. The program reads IOP_PARAMETERS_JSON and saves its result.

requires.description: Conditions that must hold when the operation is used: a platform's, or an instrument's named <device>.<id>.

source.description: A value an earlier step returned: path selects inside its result or, with view, inside a view of an array it returned

view.description: Read the value from a view of an array the step returned: field, along, at, start, stop, low, high, points, peak; path then selects inside the view. Along two axes, a map, along names both and the others give one value per axis. peak max, or min for a dip, finds the line: path ["peak", "center"] or ["peak", "width"]; level finds where the trace crosses a value: path ["crossings", 0, "at"]; fit line gives the straight line through it: path ["fit", "slope"] or ["fit", "zero"]. With one other axis not fixed, these are read at each of its positions: path ["rows", "peak", 0, "center"] (see docs/runtime/drivers.md, Reading arrays)

prominence.description: With peak, read every line that stands out by this much: path ["peaks"]

level.description: Read where the trace crosses this value, between samples, rising or falling

fit.description: Fit a straight line through the trace by least squares

sweep.description: Run this step at each value of these parameters, one point after another, the first changing slowest; what it returns is gathered into arrays over the sweep, at most 10000 points. A list gives the values (numbers, or strings as labels); start, stop and points, or center, span and points, give evenly spaced numbers. An end of a range may be read from an earlier step, as a binding is, such as where a coarse sweep found most power; each point then takes its value when it runs. With adapt, each point is placed from what the earlier ones read, closer together where the reading changes most. "${name}" takes a value from a parameter of this operation, and a bound parameter can give an end of a range

adapt.description: Place each point from what the earlier ones read: the path to the number each point reads, such as ["power"]; points come closer where it changes most (one swept parameter, 2 to 1000 points, gathered in order of value)

Place each point from what the earlier ones read: the path to the number each point reads, such as ["power"]; points come closer where it changes most (one swept parameter, 2 to 1000 points, gathered in order of value)

until.description: Stop a sweep or repetition after a point whose reading is above or below a limit, or is not a number: the later points are skipped without reaching an instrument, and the steps after the sweep run. The first point always runs

path.description: The number each point reads, in what its operation returns or in the named result of its use, such as ["current"]

above.description: Stop after a point that reads more than this, or "${name}" for a parameter

below.description: Stop after a point that reads less than this, or "${name}" for a parameter; with above, the sweep goes on while the reading stays between them
